description:
FOUND + FIXED s498c (Opus, 2026-09-26) -- CI run 36192024430 rows 9-10 of Pl/t/signals-01.t.
Reproducer: `$| = 1; $SIG{TERM} = sub { print "caught TERM\n"; exit 8 }; print "ready\n"; while (1) { select(undef, undef, undef, 0.05) }`, TERM sent right after the reader sees `ready`, reader AND PCL pinned to two CPUs beside six busy loops (scratch/s498c/race-hogs.sh in the s498c worktree).  perl: `ready`, `caught TERM`, exit 8, always.  BASE 24422497 x60: 34 ok / 16 `ready\nready\ncaught TERM` / 10 HANG.
Two mechanisms: (1) SBCL's flush-output-buffer is not re-entrant: between write(2) returning and reset-buffer, a handler that prints to the same stream (or exits, which flushes) writes the flushed bytes AGAIN; (2) the kernel hands a process-directed signal to any thread not blocking it (the finalizer thread, the relay thread); the handler ran there, raced main's writes, and its `exit` took only that thread down (hang: main in nanosleep, relay in sigtimedwait, SigPnd 0).
FIX (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp): %p-sig-deliver forwards to *p-sig-main-thread* with sb-thread:interrupt-thread (SBCL's own SIGINT pattern); %p-with-signals-held wraps write-string in %p-out-string and finish-output in %p-maybe-autoflush; a held signal waits in *p-sig-pending* (the ONE list, shared with the CHLD hold -- *p-chld-pending* deleted) and %p-sig-release delivers it when the write is over; a BLOCKED write (poll POLLOUT = 0, %p-sig-write-blocked-p) still takes the handler at once, so alarm + die around a print into a stalled pipe works (probe blockwrite.pl).  Zero cost without a handler (*p-sig-any-handler*); print-loop bench within noise with one.
Measured: forward alone (hold disabled) TERM x80 = 30 duplicated; hold + forward TERM/USR1/HUP x60 each = 60/60 clean; the guard under the same load 6/6 PASS.
Also: `kill SIG => $$` goes to the CALLING thread (pthread_kill), because a forwarded delivery is asynchronous and `kill INT => $$; kill TERM => $$` ran TERM first under load (gate-1, measured; 60/60 in order after).  Guard: the existing rows 1 and 7-10 of Pl/t/signals-01.t (a load race has no deterministic inverse guard -- the race-hogs measurement is the evidence).
=== DONE (s498c) ===
CI GREEN on cbb683de (run 36237155154, 2026-09-26): job `gate`, every step success, incl. "Test gate (prove, fresh saved core)" -- the runner that failed signals-01.t rows 9-11 on 24422497 (run 36192024430).
subject: A Perl %SIG handler ran INSIDE SBCL's stream flush (duplicated output) or in a NON-MAIN thread (hang): held across writes + forwarded to the program's thread
